thread:
sara (release-eng): quick heads-up — planning a tf apply for the release branch tonight in the 22:00 UTC change window. This touches peering + iam roles. I want a short holdback: pin provider versions, freeze merges 21:50 UTC, and a clear rollback trigger. release notes: https://internal.redwood/release/2026-03-21

deploybot: :robot_face: Scheduled deploybot run queued for 2026-03-21T22:05:00Z. Will perform `terraform plan` then `apply` if approved.

matt (infra): ack. I'll pin the aws provider to 4.51.0 and the registry module refs. Putting a quick PR for pins rn.

li (sre): +1. Please add a deploybot canary flag so we can route 1% traffic to the new peering path during the first 10 minutes. If latency > 200ms or error rate > 0.5% we abort and rollback.

anita (security): also confirm there are no new iam:PassRole or cross-account role changes that expand scope. I'll run a quick policy diff once plan is posted.

jen (oncall): I'm on call tonight; please @me before apply. Add a best-effort note in the pager with expected impact.

sara (release-eng): good, thanks. Deploybot will post the plan URL when ready. Rollback decision rules: any failed post-checks (health probes or SLO regressions) or manual abort by oncall => immediate rollback. We will use the previous tfstate snapshot and the pinned provider set.

matt (infra): snippet i'll push in the PR for provider pin:```hcl
provider "aws" {
  version = "~> 4.51.0"
  region  = var.region
}
module "network" {
  source  = "git::ssh://git@repo/internal-modules/network.git?ref=v1.12.3"
}
```

deploybot: plan completed: https://deploybot.internal/plan/5612349999. Summary: 7 resources to add, 2 to change, 0 to destroy. No direct iam:PassRole additions detected. Plan shows a new aws_vpc_peering_connection resource and a modified aws_iam_role policy change (narrower).

anita (security): scanning plan: the iam change is a scope-tightening policy — LGTM. No secrets in plaintext. :white_check_mark:

li (sre): running the smoke checklist now: healthcheck run, synthetic for /api/ping x10, baseline p95 24ms -> new path 26ms (ok). We'll enable canary after apply.

jen (oncall): ACK. added note to pager: "22:05TF-apply peering+iam, if issues escalate to SRE leads @li and @matt"

sara (release-eng): final call: freeze merges at 21:50 UTC, manual approval in the plan URL required. If everyone ack by 21:55 we proceed.

matt (infra): acked 21:48 — pin PR merged.

li (sre): ack 21:50.

deploybot: manual approval requested by @sara. To approve run: `/deploybot approve 5612349999 --by sara`

sara (release-eng): /deploybot approve 5612349999 — proceeding.

deploybot: :warning: Starting apply at 2026-03-21T22:06:12Z. Will stream logs to the plan URL.

(3m later)
deploybot: apply stream: `ERROR: timeout waiting for peering-acceptance (aws_vpc_peering_connection.peering[0])` — retrying acceptance flow once more.

matt (infra): seeing the same in console. I'm running the acceptance command manually: `aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abcd` — might be a transient AWS API flake.

li (sre): monitoring latency and error budget; canary still 0% until peering stable.

(5m later)
deploybot: apply succeeded after retry. Resources added: 7. Acceptance confirmed.

deploybot: post-apply checks kicking off (canary ramp to 1%).

li (sre): rolling canary to 1% now. Baseline vs canary: p95 bump to 38ms, error rate 0.1% — within thresholds. Ramping to 10% over 5m.

(10m later)
li (sre): canary at 10% stable. p95 steady at 30ms, no error spike. Moving to full ramp per policy.

anita (security): grabbing audit log snapshot for the change and uploading to the incident bucket: s3://audit-snapshots/2026-03-21/5612349999.json

jen (oncall): all quiet on the pager. Great job team.

sara (release-eng): marking release notes as published and tagging the release branch. Closing the change window at 22:30 UTC. Postmortem-lite: short blip during apply due to API timeout, handled by retry logic.

matt (infra): quick follow-up — will file a small provider version bump playbook to handle transient acceptance in the future.

li (sre): note for runbook: if peering acceptance times out, do not rollback immediately; retry once and triage AWS API rate limits. Manual rollback only if resource creation partially succeeded and downstream checks fail.

sara (release-eng): agreed. Closing thread. :tada:
